new_cores.summary: A half-angle plane rotation by the negative exact split angle sends a column pair (x,y) to (sqrt(x^2+y^2),0); the zero pair uses angle 0 and needs no division.
Mixing two rows by (a,b),(c,d) scales the determinant by a*d-b*c; for a plane rotation this factor is cos^2+sin^2=1, so the determinant is preserved.
Reversing a chronological list of plane rotations and negating every angle exactly inverts the sequence, by a single-step inverse law plus list induction.
A bottom-up adjacent sweep zeros a column strictly below its top window row while leaving rows outside the window untouched, by a zeroing induction protected by outside-invariance.
An orthonormal matrix with a column supported only on its diagonal has that pivot squaring to 1; a nonnegative-pivot guarantee pins it to exactly +1.
An orthogonal det-1 matrix whose first N-1 columns are the identity prefix must be the identity; the determinant hypothesis pins the final diagonal to +1 rather than a -1 reflection.
Consecutive binary-reflected Gray indices differ by exactly one physical wire flip, proved by width induction with parity-split head/tail casework.
The accumulated rotation transform is orthogonal with determinant 1, so its transpose times the upper-trapezoidal residual recovers the original rectangular matrix exactly.
Folding a left boundary vector into the first core of a matrix-product chain gives a scalar amplitude equal to the left-weighted sum of open-chain amplitudes, via a finite double-sum exchange.
Absorbing the right boundary vector into the last core of a matrix-product chain (terminal bond 1) reproduces the chronological matrix-vector readout at every incoming bond, by induction.
A matrix-product chain of n cores with bonds at most D stores at most 2*n*D^2 scalars; this is a stored-address count and not a bound on contraction arithmetic.
Processing one more column advances the elimination's upper-prefix staircase from index k to k+1 (fresh column cleared, earlier zeros preserved), so after M columns the residual is upper-trapezoidal.

A deterministic thin factorization exists for every real matrix with inner dimension exactly min(m,n); the orthonormal-row factor satisfies Q*Q^T=I in both wide (transpose elimination) and tall (R=A, Q=I) regimes, with no rank hypothesis.

A greedy transposition process extending a finite injection agrees with the target injection on every original index, proved by a strengthened induction using injectivity to protect earlier placements.

Reorienting an orthogonal matrix to determinant 1 by a single sign-flip chosen from column-permutation parity yields an orthogonal det-1 matrix on both parity branches, without ever evaluating the determinant.
Symmetric Gray-coordinate relabeling of a matrix preserves orthogonality and the determinant exactly, because one shared row/column bijection makes it a multiplicative identity-fixing reindexing.

Reindexing an adjacent plane rotation by the Gray labeling equals a selected RY two-level plane on the Gray-flip wire; the half-angle is theta or -theta according to the first index's target bit, from the pair ordering.
Two basis states share a selected RY plane's control context if and only if they are equal or related by a single target-wire X, pinning the exact 2D pair the rotation can touch.

Per selected-rotation gate counts (2^c RY, 2*(2^c-1) CX, no oracle) do not make a full SO matrix linear in dimension: a quadratic number of planes times per-plane cost is cubic, shown with a q=1 witness.
Iterated step-by-step application of a plane-rotation list equals one multiplication by the accumulated matrix taken in reverse list order; the reverse order is forced by first-listed-acts-first.
The three-bit source loader s |-> s XOR 3 is an involution with image list [3,2,1,0,7,6,5,4]; XOR-with-mask self-inversion is the circuit-level undoing of the two bit-flip gates.

The reversible access circuit's clean-action theorem bundles three independent guarantees (correct sum, preserved row, restored work=0) and all three hold only under the work=0 hypothesis; a dirty work wire voids both correctness and restoration.

Definitional resource faithfulness certifies accounting consistency (not optimality), zero oracle calls certifies full primitive synthesis of a fixed three-bit witness, and importing an oracle-bearing theory is never itself an oracle-realized claim.

The compiled primitive-gate product equals the permutation matrix of the reversible program's basis bijection; this refinement links the low-level pipeline to the combinatorial map and forces a 0/1 permutation structure.
A real planar rotation [[c,-s],[s,c]] over C is unitary exactly when c^2+s^2=1: the off-diagonals of the Gram matrix cancel identically and conjugation is trivial on real entries.

The inverse-cosine amplitude gate is unitary for every real parameter and for any extension of the angle, but its clean-entry readout equals the parameter only on [-1,1]; for |x|>1 the readout cannot equal x because cosine is bounded in [-1,1], proved without guessing the extension.

A block-diagonal operator built from per-block unitaries is unitary: the conjugate transpose respects the block structure, multiplication is pointwise in the control index, and each block collapses to the identity.

Relabelling a unitary's basis by a single bijection on both rows and columns preserves unitarity, because conjugate transpose and multiplication commute with the reindexing algebra equivalence and the identity reindexes to the identity.

Lifting a selector PREPARE to the full register as I ⊗ (PREPARE ⊗ I) preserves unitarity by applying the Kronecker-product-of-unitaries law twice; identities on untouched registers are inert unitaries.

A controlled SELECT (coeff,(s,x)) |-> (coeff,(s,p_s(x))) is a bijection with inverse applying (p_s)^{-1} under the same preserved selector s, hence unitary as a basis permutation; coherent control requires carrying the selector through for inversion.

Composition of basis-permutation matrices multiplies them in reverse order (second times first realizes first-then-second), because each column's single 1 collapses the product to function composition and left action forces the reversal.

The full PREPARE-dagger/SELECT/AMPLITUDE/PREPARE composite is unitary by combining four local certificates through unitary-group closure; the unprepare stage must be the adjoint of PREPARE to uncompute it and inherit unitarity.

In the LCU clean projected entry the SELECT indicator p_s(y)=x is equivalent to (p_s)^{-1}(x)=y by bijectivity, and the PREPARE amplitude enters as conj(PREPARE[s,s0])*PREPARE[s,s0] = |PREPARE[s,s0]|^2, a nonnegative weight from the adjoint/plain sandwich.

The clean PREPARE-bra projection pins coefficient and system while coherently summing the selector with weights conj(PREPARE[s,s0]); the sum adds amplitudes (interference possible), unlike an incoherent classical mixture of probabilities.

Every complex matrix A = H1 + i H2 with H1=(A+A-dagger)/2 and H2=(A-A-dagger)/(2i) both Hermitian; the proof needs conj(2i)=-2i and i/(2i) cancellation, mirroring z = Re(z) + i Im(z) at the matrix level.

The Hermitian part S1 of the homogenized S = [[A,B],[0,0]] has zero lower-right and B/2 upper-right with no hypothesis, but its lower-left block is B-dagger/2 in general and only equals B/2 when B is Hermitian; the hypothesis is used exactly to rewrite conj(B[j,i]) as B[i,j].

Two equal pi filler phases leave a nonzero lower-right clean entry -N_A that cannot match S1's zero block for nonzero normalizer; replacing one phase by 0 cancels the filler while preserving the A, A-dagger, B clean blocks.

H = S1(x)X + S2(x)I is Hermitian from three closure facts (tensor, identity, sum of Hermitians), with no dimension or commutation hypotheses because the tensor Hermiticity check factorizes per register and Hermiticity is a per-matrix symmetry.

The ten-block paper transcript asserts only block identity and order (no matrices, cleanup, unitarity, or correctness), the SWAP is a label-only placeholder whose semantics live elsewhere, and the layout's 9 declared signal qubits differ from the effective 10 the clean projection pins.

The indicator-oracle bundle certifies U is a permutation of a self-inverse label map, so U^2 = I and U-dagger = U; dagger-equals-itself plus self-inverse image make the same oracle its own exact clean uncompute, which permutation-ness alone (P-dagger = P^{-1} not P) would not guarantee.
A homomorphism automatically preserves the identity and inverses, which is exactly why a representation phi satisfies phi(e)=1_V and phi(g^{-1})=phi(g)^{-1} with invertibility free.
Averaging an arbitrary inner product over a finite group yields a G-invariant inner product making the representation unitary, so orthogonal complements of invariant subspaces are invariant.
Averaging a projection over the group produces an equivariant projection onto the invariant subspace whose kernel is an invariant complement, provided |G| is invertible in the field.
A nonzero equivariant map between irreducibles must be an isomorphism, because its kernel and image are invariant subspaces and irreducibility leaves only the trivial options.

Over an algebraically closed field an equivariant endomorphism of an irrep is a scalar, because f minus an eigenvalue is non-invertible and equivariant hence zero; consequently the commutant of an irrep is the scalars.
For an abelian group each operator commutes with all others, so Schur over C makes it a scalar and every vector spans an invariant line, forcing complex irreps to be one-dimensional.

The Pauli twirl of any qubit state equals the maximally mixed state because the twirled operator commutes with an irreducible representation (so is a scalar by Schur) and the trace fixes the scalar to 1/2.
The character is a class function because cyclicity of the trace kills conjugation, and its value at the identity equals the dimension of the representation.
Character orthonormality turns multiplicities into inner products n_i = (chi_i, chi_V), from which irreducibility (norm-squared one) and the isomorphism-iff-equal-characters criterion follow.
The multiplicity of an irreducible U in V equals dim Hom_G(U, V): additivity splits the intertwiner space, Schur makes self-intertwiners one-dimensional and cross-intertwiners zero.

Group-averaging an operator produces an equivariant operator that, on a multiplicity-free decomposition into two inequivalent irreps, is block diagonal with scalar diagonal blocks (Schur ii) and vanishing off-diagonal blocks (Schur i).
The swap operator is a G-commuting involution whose +-1 eigenspace projectors (1 +- F)/2 are complementary orthogonal projections onto the invariant symmetric and antisymmetric squares.

Averaging the representation over G gives the orthogonal projection onto the invariant vectors V^G, whose trace counts the trivial-representation multiplicity, the trivial case of the character projection formula.

When an isotypical component has multiplicity greater than one, the symmetrized operator's diagonal block is identity-on-irrep tensor an arbitrary multiplicity-space operator, so it need not be a scalar - a concrete S_2 swap counterexample.
The tensor square of an irreducible representation of dimension at least two is reducible, because the swap operator splits it into nonzero invariant symmetric and antisymmetric subspaces.

Isotypical components are unique but splitting a multiplicity-greater-than-one component into individual irreducible subspaces is not, as shown by two distinct trivial-line splittings of the symmetric subspace of (C^2)^{(x)2}.

The averaging that makes representations unitary needs finiteness or compactness; the shear representation of (R,+) has an invariant line with no invariant complement, so it is not completely reducible.

Schur part (ii) fails without algebraic closure: a rotation gives an irreducible real representation whose commutant is C, not the real scalars, while part (i)'s division-algebra conclusion still holds.

Averaging-based results (invariant complements, complete reducibility, character orthonormality) transfer from finite to compact groups via the Haar integral, but |G|-explicit identities fail and finite-dimensionality of irreducibles becomes the Peter-Weyl theorem.

The dual representation is phi(g^{-1})^T (the conjugate when unitary), self-dual exactly when the character is real-valued; the omega-representation of Z/3 is a non-self-dual irrep, and duality always preserves irreducibility.
Implementing a POVM through shared-beta block encodings of sqrt(P_i) gives postselection success probability exactly 1/(beta^2 2^m), with completeness collapsing the state-dependent sum.
After postselection the POVM circuit yields outcome i with probability <psi|P_i|psi> and the correct sqrt(P_i)-update, with the mixed-state rule following by linearity.
Amplitude amplification turns the 1/(beta^2 2^m) single-shot success into a constant using O(beta 2^{m/2} log(1/delta)) queries to W and W^dagger, a quadratic gain over naive repetition.

Unambiguous discrimination of overlapping states is impossible with only two conclusive outcomes (completeness forces trace > 2); the inconclusive P_? is the structural slack that restores a valid POVM.
The two-conclusive-one-inconclusive discrimination POVM is valid: P_? = I - P_psi - P_phi stays PSD because P_psi+P_phi has operator norm exactly 1.

The 'same ancilla a / same beta' hypotheses of Lemma 9.15 are load-bearing: dropping common beta reweights the measured effects by 1/beta_i^2; dropping the shared ancilla destroys the single success-flag projector.

The amplitude oracle is built by load-angle / controlled-rotate / uncompute-angle; the final (O'_A)^{-1} is mandatory because discarding the entangled work register would decohere the amplitude and spoil downstream interference.

The amplitude oracle is valid exactly for |A_ij| <= 1 (|A_ij| = 1 is legitimate, only the sqrt term vanishes); ||A||_max < 1 is a sufficient convenience, not a necessity, and only |A_ij| > 1 is excluded.

The bit oracle is a digital/query interface and the amplitude oracle an analog interface; the latter is derived via query + controlled rotation + inverse query, with the work register borrowed clean, not consumed.

The amplitude oracle is a (1,1)-block-encoding of a diagonal matrix (<0|<i|O_A|0>|j> = A_ii delta_ij); the construction's alpha = 1 is globally optimal only when ||A|| = 1, not for every diagonal A with ||A|| < 1.
An s-regular bipartite sparsity pattern splits into s perfect matchings (Koenig), giving A = sum_ell A^{(ell)} of 1-sparse pieces and an equal-weight LCU block encoding with alpha = s.

Propagating source and (Hermitian-D) target through the sparse LCU circuit gives <0|<0^s|<i|U_A|0>|0^s>|j> = (1/s)A_ij, with the success flag dropping the |1> branch and delta_{i,c(j,ell)} selecting one matching.
The two-oracle (O_r, O_c) sparse model gives <0|<0^n|<i|U_A|0>|0^n>|j> = (1/s)A_ij; the paired deltas enforce row/column consistency so arbitrary rotations on zero entries never contribute.

A Hermitian A need not have a Hermitian block encoding -- only the encoded block is Hermitian; Definition 9.23's U_A = U_A^dagger is a strictly stronger condition that enables the qubitization reflection structure.
Fig. 9.9 produces a Hermitian block encoding: the matched term is (1/s)sqrt(A_ij)sqrt(A_ji)^*, and Hermiticity A_ji = A_ij^* recombines it to (1/s)A_ij, giving U_A in HBE_{s,n+2}(A).

The induced block A~ = ((Xi')_{N'})^dagger U_A Xi_N has entries <psi_i|U_A|phi_j> and equals the compression Pi' U_A Pi in the chosen bases; ||A - alpha A~|| <= eps generalizes the computational-basis definition.
For Hermitian A, the singular value transformation equals the eigenvalue transformation when f has definite parity: odd f uses the sign(D) factor to recover signs, even f ignores them.

The dilation A~ = [[0,A^dagger],[A,0]] has eigenvalues pm sigma_i with eigenvectors |z_i^pm>; an eigenvalue transform of A~ realizes the SVT of A, with a deterministic ancilla outcome fixed by parity.

Matrix powers A^k are generally not singular value transformations because A^2 = W Sigma (V^dagger W) Sigma V^dagger has an irreducible interior unitary; the inverse is the exceptional odd SVT A^{-1} = V Sigma^{-1} W^dagger.

For a Hermitian block encoding, each eigenvector is qubitized into a 2D subspace where U_A is a reflection and O = U_A Z_Pi a rotation; O^k has top-left T_k(lambda_i), so (U_A Z_Pi)^k block-encodes the Chebyshev polynomial T_k(A).

In an eight-counter exact-real operation model, prove a stored two-row plane rotation on length-M rows costs exactly 6*M field, 10*M read and 6*M write operations, accounting for each from the three materialized passes.
Prove one stored rotation step costs 6*M field, 10*M+2*N+2 read and 6*M+2*N write operations, where the 2*N spine-copy term is a stipulated charge of the cost contract.
By induction on step count, prove a k-step column sweep is bounded by k*(step budget + emit) on every counter and emits exactly k records including zero-angle steps.
By list induction, prove a stored replay of L recorded rotations denotes the product of plane rotations (not formed densely) and costs L times a per-step budget plus one trailing read.
Prove the eight per-counter polynomial budgets of a stored rectangular compilation sum to N*M*(22*M+30*N+29)+5*N*N+4*N+M+1 and read it as an exact-real, not finite-bit, count.
Prove a stored wide thin-LQ factorization costs the sum of transpose, compile, and two extraction budgets per counter, and the same run yields exact A=R*Q with orthonormal Q.
Prove a size-k monadic sum of equal-cost summands costs k*(B+one field), and specialize to a bond-D contraction entry costing D*(three reads + two field).
Prove the stored chain closure costs 20*D-squared+30*D+5*n-squared+7*n+constant, explaining the n-squared term as a reference-copy series and the n-independent left closure.
By chain induction, prove the stored Gram-environment computation costs at most n*(24*D-cubed+25*D-squared+20*D+6)+5*D-squared+4*D+6, with the cubic term from the per-node contractions.
Prove the stored tensor-train norm costs the Gram cost plus exactly two reads and one square root (total +3), and equals the Euclidean norm of the represented vector.
Prove the sum-over-tags total equals the eight-term enumerated total, is additive, zero on the zero cost and one on a unit charge, and explain why this enables compositional cost proofs.
Prove the four named integer counters of the stored Hermite raw-source run sum to 2*n-squared+10*n+7, and delineate the same-run scope excluding finite-bit runtime and normalization.
Prove a primitive circuit's parallel-scheduling depth is at most its gate count via the per-step inequality that one gate raises every wire depth by at most one.
Counterexample: materialization cost is not a dimensions-only polynomial because it keeps the supplier's double-sum work; a clean bound needs a uniform per-entry supplier bound.
Counterexample (x=y=0): the angle routine makes zero inverse-cosine calls on the zero branch, so the branch-independent budget is an upper bound, not an exact per-call cost.
Boundary: the stored identity costs 5*N*N+4*N exact-real operations, nonzero for all N at least 1, free only at the degenerate N=0.
Counterexample: persistent log append costs the left length in reads and writes and is independent of the right length, so it is neither constant nor total-length dependent.
Boundary: the tall LQ branch (m>n) runs no sweep, returning the input plus an identity at cost one comparison + 5*n*n+4*n, refuting that thin-LQ always eliminates.
Counterexample: exponential calls are n+2 plus guard-dependent injections (range n+2 to 3*n+4), so the always-two-per-stage formula is only the worst case, not the exact count.
Boundary: the stored chain's maximum bond is at most max(D,1); the floor of one is the scalar-boundary degenerate case (D=0), and the bound is structural, separate from construction cost.
A single Taylor-truncation polynomial reproduces every prescribed derivative up to order k exactly, via the j! normalization of Taylor coefficients.
A zero of multiplicity k+1 in p-q forces all derivatives through order k to agree at the point, with the bound sharp at order k+1.
The source Hermite bridge polynomial is strictly positive on [-1,0] because its generating-series coefficients are nonnegative with constant term one.
Two degree-<=2k+1 polynomials with matching k-jets at both endpoints coincide, by coprime endpoint moduli and a degree-count against the combined multiplicity 2k+2.
The product (x+1)^{k+1} x^{k+1} of degree 2k+2 carries all-zero endpoint k-jets, proving the degree-2k+1 bound in the uniqueness theorem is necessary and sharp.
The exp times negative-binomial generating series has coefficient sum_m C(k+r-m,k)/m!, which is nonnegative and equals 1 at degree 0.
The source bridge is a symmetric sum of two order-(k+1) endpoint-decoupled terms in the coordinate t=p+1, each delivering one node's value via A_k(0)=1.
Each source monomial t^i(1-t)^{k+1} degree-elevates exactly into the degree-2k+1 Bernstein basis with weights C(k-i,j)/C(2k+1,i+j), yielding a nonnegative Bernstein coefficient vector.
Left de Casteljau subdivision at u reparametrises a Bernstein polynomial to u*t exactly, proved by a semiconjugacy of the linear step operator iterated d times.
De Casteljau subinterval restriction keeps every Bernstein coefficient inside the original range, because each new coefficient is a convex combination (partition of unity plus nonnegativity).
The discrete squared mass of polynomial samples on an arithmetic grid equals a degree-sized Faulhaber combination of power sums, an exact identity independent of the sample count.
The exponential-tail discrete squared mass is a geometric sum whose closed form requires an explicit step=0 branch where the common ratio is one, with both branches agreeing in the limit.
The unnormalized sample norm is at least 1 uniformly in order, width and scale, because the central grid point sits at the splice where the target equals 1.
An additive polynomial array q(u(x)+v(y)) factorizes with inner dimension deg(q)+1 via shifted Taylor coefficients, bounding its rank by the degree alone.
Finite-width factorizations form an algebra: sum adds widths, Hadamard product multiplies them, negation and scaling preserve them, letting composite width bounds be assembled symbolically.
The full exponential-polynomial-exponential sample array has cut rank at most 8k+12, assembled as 2 + 4(2k+2) + 2 from indicator, exponential, and polynomial finite-width factorizations.

A per-cut rank bound of 8k+12 is a separation certificate, not a construction; preparation still needs factor isometrization, angles, and true normalization, so the rank bound alone does not close the task.
C^k gluing of two pieces needs derivative agreement at every order through k, not just value matching; ReLU (f=0, g=x) matches values yet fails C^1 at the cut.
The exponential-polynomial-exponential target is globally C^k for every k, proved by applying a reusable two-piece gluing theorem at both junctions using the Hermite endpoint jets.
An exact-real-interval binary search returns the true tail/bridge cutoff index for every width and scale, with endpoint and single-cell boundary cases, using 2n field operations and n+1 comparisons.
With a Hermitian block encoding, one qubitization iterate O = U R is a plane rotation whose square has top-left entry 2t^2-1, so O^2 block-encodes the degree-two Chebyshev polynomial 2A^2-I.

When the block-encoding unitary is not Hermitian, U maps the eigenvector plane to a different plane, so the adjoint-paired iterate adjoint(U) R U R is needed to return; its powers give even Chebyshev orders and one extra U R gives odd orders.

Powering the plane rotation produces first-kind Chebyshev on the diagonal and second-kind Chebyshev times sqrt(1-t^2) off-diagonal; the prefactor forces the off-diagonal to vanish at the spectral endpoints.

Even singular value transformations use the right singular vectors on both sides, while odd ones send right vectors to left vectors; the swap happens because each U application exchanges the two singular-vector planes and parity counts the swaps.

For the non-normal nilpotent, the degree-two singular value transformation is diag(-1,1) from singular values 1 and 0, not minus the identity predicted by its zero eigenvalues; the construction acts on singular values.

Sub-blocks of a unitary have singular values in [0,1] and admit a cosine-sine structure with C^2+S^2=I, which pins every Chebyshev argument into [-1,1] and keeps the trigonometric polynomial representation valid.

The flag reflection built from Z is diagonal in the flag/complement grading so it commutes with the block-diagonal outer unitaries; an X-based reflection is off-diagonal, fails to commute, and destroys the clean cosine-sine factorization.

A direct index-controlled select of even Chebyshev transforms costs order K^2 base-unitary queries, but reusing one squared iterate across the binary digits of the index costs only 2K-2 queries, equal to a single top-order term.

A parity-mixed polynomial splits uniquely into even and odd parts, each separately block-encodable; recombining them with one balanced-control ancilla realizes f(A) but doubles the subnormalization factor because the two-branch superposition halves the success amplitude.

A definite-parity degree-d Chebyshev polynomial is block-encoded with subnormalization equal to the coefficient 1-norm, about log d extra ancillas, and order d queries to the block-encoding unitary and its adjoint, kept distinct from gate and preparation costs.

Qubitization beyond the computational basis is a product of two projector reflections; equal input/output ranks reduce it to the ordinary iterate, and unequal ranks still admit the two-dimensional rotation analysis because any two-reflection product splits into at most two-dimensional invariant planes.

In the identity-unitary two-qubit example the encoded operator is cosine theta times the identity and the two-reflection iterate is a rotation by twice theta, whose eigenphases plus/minus 2 theta encode the singular value cosine theta.

The Grover iterate is a product of two planar reflections whose axes differ by the half-angle (arcsine of 1/sqrt(N)), so it is a rotation by the full angle; its k-th power gives marked amplitude sine of (2k+1) half-angles.
The optimal iteration count bounds Grover's single-run failure probability by 4/N; detectable failure plus geometric repetition keeps the expected oracle-query cost at order sqrt(N).

With M known marked states the uniform state's half-angle has sine sqrt(M/N), so the optimal iteration count scales as sqrt(N/M); an unknown M leaves the rotation angle unknown and a fixed iteration count over- or under-rotates.

Grover search is an odd Chebyshev singular value transformation of the scalar 1/sqrt(N): the flagged odd iterate is T_{2k+1}(a) times the uniform-to-marked map, equal to (-1)^k sine of (2k+1) half-angles, matching the Grover amplitude up to a global phase.

The identity T_{2k+1}(a) = (-1)^k sine((2k+1) arcsine a) holds only on [-1,1]; for a greater than one it fails concretely (T_3(2)=26 against a bounded sine) and must be replaced by the hyperbolic-cosine form.

Classical unstructured search needs at least N-1 worst-case queries because padding leaves two unqueried candidates with identical all-zero evidence, capping success at one half; the classical-transcript counting gives no quantum bound, which is only order sqrt(N).

Running the bit oracle on an answer qubit in the minus state imprints the sign (minus one) to the f(x) on the input and returns the answer qubit unchanged, so one phase reflection costs one bit-oracle query plus a one-time reusable minus-state preparation with no measurement.

Amplitude amplification rotates the good-subspace amplitude by order sqrt(p) per iteration, reaching constant success in order 1/sqrt(p) iterations versus 1/p classical trials; the quadratic speedup is because amplitude grows linearly in steps while measured probability is its square.
The isotropic family rho(x) has unit trace for all x and is positive exactly on [0, d^2/(d^2-1)], each endpoint tight because one of its two distinct eigenvalues vanishes there.

From the monotone extendibility thresholds one reads off that d>=3 Werner states are 2-extendible, the largest isotropic extension order is floor(1/(1 - x(d+1)/d)), and separability is the hold-for-all-k limit x >= d/(d+1).

The converse of channel-preserved extendibility fails: the depolarizing channel sends the non-2-extendible Phi+ to a 2-extendible isotropic state, so a channel can create extendibility the input lacked.
The de Finetti d-vs-d^2 gap comes from purifying onto a d^2-dimensional local system; both bounds vanish exactly when k = o(n), the mixed case needing d-times larger n for the same accuracy.
A single cloning unitary can serve a pair only if the states are orthogonal or equal, since unitarity forces the overlap to satisfy z = z^2; e.g. |0> and |+> cannot be cloned.
The optimal cloner's fidelity d_N/d_M exceeds 1 - Kd/N (tending to 1 for fixed K), and because it is input-independent its worst-case and Haar-average fidelities coincide, making it optimal for both.

The normalized Young diagram lambda/n is always a valid spectrum, and because relative entropy vanishes only at the true r the exponential bound dominates the polynomial prefactor, giving Pr(hat r != r) -> 0.

Separable states are infinitely extendible via index-shared copies on each B_j, and k-extendibility descends to all k' <= k by discarding systems, yielding the monogamy inclusion chain Ext_1 superset ... superset SEP.

A purification Schmidt-decomposed across (AB : B'C) whose AB-marginal is the rank-one psi_AB must collapse to a single term, forcing rho_{A B B'} = psi_AB tensor omega_{B'} and ruling out 2-extensions of pure entangled states.
Applying the channel independently to each B_i of a k-extension yields a k-extension of (id tensor N)(rho_AB); CP gives positivity and TP gives both unit trace and the marginal-reduction identity.
The maximally entangled state satisfies the transpose trick (X tensor I)|Phi+> = (I tensor X^T)|Phi+> in the fixed basis, which forces its invariance under every U tensor conj(U).
Averaging |phi><phi|^{tensor n} over Haar pure states gives, by irreducibility of U^{tensor n} on Sym^n and Schur's lemma, exactly (1/d_sym) Pi_sym, with the constant fixed by the trace.

The symmetric-projection cloner has input-independent fidelity d_N/d_M for every pure state, because phi^{tensor M} is Pi_M-invariant and |phi><phi| is an idempotent of unit trace, so it saturates the optimal-cloning bound.

Haar-twirling a channel yields a U^{tensor n}-covariant map because the invariance substitution W = UV absorbs the rotation, and this covariance is what lets Schur-Weyl duality pin the output on the symmetric subspace.

Because rho^{tensor n} is permutation invariant and spectra are unitarily invariant, spectrum-estimation effects may be taken permutation- and U^{tensor n}-invariant WLOG, which the Schur-Weyl projectors {P_lambda} realize as a complete measurement commuting with both symmetries.

A Young projector e_T kills every tensor basis vector whose symbol frequencies are not majorized by its shape lambda, because the f_q most frequent symbols must occupy distinct columns, forcing the majorization partial-sum inequalities.

Because the symmetric projector absorbs permutations (Pi_n Q_pi = Pi_n), the symmetrization average collapses and Pi_n rhobar Pi_n = Pi_n rho Pi_n, so symmetric-subspace compression cannot distinguish a state from its symmetrization.

The symmetric-projection cloner is completely positive (composition of the CP embedding and CP compression) and trace non-increasing because Pi_M <= I, with the trace preserved exactly on symmetric pure-power inputs phi^{tensor N}.
The de Finetti fidelity ratio factorizes into d-1 increasing terms, so replacing them by the smallest, applying Bernoulli, and a crude comparison yields the clean lower bound 1 - kd/m.

A stars-and-bars count gives dim Sym^n(C^d) = binom(n+d-1,n), a degree-(d-1) polynomial that vanishes against d^n, explaining why the symmetric-subspace-based de Finetti and cloning constructions are so effective.
The commutant of End(V) tensor 1 inside End(V tensor W) is exactly 1 tensor End(W), proved by a block-matrix argument.
For an isotypical representation the commutant is the sum of multiplicity-space endomorphism algebras and the double commutant recovers A.
External product representations of a direct product act with independent factors; irreducibility and exhaustion follow from character factorization and conjugacy-class counting.
The permutation and diagonal-unitary algebras on a tensor power are each other's commutants, proved via a polynomial-in-t interpolation argument.
Operators commuting with all tensor-factor permutations under conjugation are combinations of tensor powers of single endomorphisms, via the operator symmetric subspace.
The symmetric subspace of a tensor power is spanned by the n-fold powers of single vectors, proved by polarization and a closedness argument.
Young diagrams with more than d rows contribute nothing to the tensor power of C^d because column antisymmetrization annihilates every vector with a forced repeated label.
The antisymmetrizer on the n-fold tensor power of C^d is identically zero when n exceeds d, since no wedge of n distinct basis vectors exists.
The Young symmetrizer annihilates a tensor basis vector exactly when the sorted content vector is not majorized by the shape, via column-strict feasibility.
Explicit Schur-Weyl dimension count for the fourth power of C^3 verifying eighty-one equals the sum of products of the two piece dimensions over the four admissible diagrams.
The two-dimensional unitary irreducible piece for a two-part partition has dimension lambda_1 minus lambda_2 plus one, from both tableau counting and the determinant-times-symmetric-power form.
The hook length formula gives thirty-five standard tableaux for shape (4,2,1) and exactly one for a single row or single column of n boxes.
Permutations are conjugate exactly when they share a cycle type, proved via the identity that conjugation relabels cycle entries by the conjugating permutation.
The second tensor power of C^d splits into symmetric and antisymmetric eigenspaces of the swap with dimensions d(d+1)/2 and d(d-1)/2 summing to d squared.
Twirling sends any state to a twirl-invariant Werner state whose visibility, measured against the swap, equals that of the original state.
A Werner state is entangled exactly when its visibility is negative, shown via the partial transpose of the swap having a negative eigenvalue and a separable preparation otherwise.
Multipartite states invariant under the diagonal unitary action are linear combinations of factor-permutation operators, by the mutual-commutant theorem.
Permutation-invariant operators on the tensor power of a fixed-dimension system are determined by only polynomially many parameters, via Schur-Weyl blocks and polynomial dimension bounds.
The Schur-Weyl block weights of a tensor-power density operator concentrate for large n on diagrams whose normalized rows match the spectrum, at a relative-entropy decay rate.
A bipartite state is isotropic exactly when its partial transpose is a Werner state, via transport of the symmetry group through partial transposition.

Refutes uniqueness of the dilating unitary: a rotation and a reflection share the same clean entry x, so a clean-block (or clean-action) certificate pins U only on the clean sub-block and leaves the garbage branch free; A does not determine U or its cost.
Describes the four LCU stages (prepare/amplitude/select/unprepare), their registers, and why unprepare must be the adjoint of prepare on the shared selector ancilla.
Proves the pointwise equivalence between the projected-block certificate and the clean-basis-action certificate via column selection, and extends it to arbitrary inputs by linearity.

Derives the exact clean projected entry of the logical LCU matrix as a selector sum with SELECT matching indicator and conjugate-times-itself PREPARE weights, explaining the |prepare|^2 selection probability and the shared selector register.

Computes the all-zero postselection success probability ||A v||^2/alpha^2 of a block encoding from unitarity and the projected-block contract, and derives the 1/alpha query cost and normalizer charge.
Uses the 2x2 scalar dilation to derive the sharp |x|<=1 orthogonality boundary and the contraction lower bound: a normalizer-1 clean block cannot encode a scalar of magnitude above 1.

Refutes the claim that the one-sparse route encodes any one-nonzero-per-column matrix: a two-nonzero column violates the fixed-support hypothesis, while a zero-amplitude column is reconstructed exactly.

Shows the all-(-1) LCU filler phases give lower-right clean entry -N and so cannot equal S1 (whose lower-right block is 0) for nonzero normalizer, and gives the phase-balanced correction that recovers S1.

Proves a bijective index map yields a rational-orthogonal permutation unitary (injectivity for columns, surjectivity for rows) and derives its 0/1 partial-permutation clean block and expressiveness limit.

Explains the free exact-to-zero-error-approximate repackaging (reusing the pointwise clean-block proof as the epsilon=0 bound) and the boundary that an operator-norm statement still needs a pointwise-to-norm bridge theorem.

Let P permute computational-basis labels and let a circuit have chronological matrices U1,...,Ut. Prove that consistently renaming every wire realizes P(Ut...U1)P inverse rather than inserting a physical permutation gate. Explain why output-only relabeling would fail to preserve circuit multiplication.

A circuit uses only single-qubit rotations, bit flips and controlled bit flips. A bijection relabels all physical wires, preserving which wire controls which target. Which of total instruction count, rotation count and controlled-bit-flip count must stay unchanged? Does this alone prove equal nearest-neighbor routing cost on fixed hardware?

Define R(theta)=[[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]]. Derive the exact operator distance between R(a) and R(b), and prove it is at most |a-b|/2. Why does adding any number of untouched spectator qubits not multiply the distance by a dimension factor?

For the real rotation R(theta)=[[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]], compare R(theta+2pi) and R(theta). A colleague claims the two full operators have distance0 because every output probability agrees. Refute or prove that claim, and distinguish bare-system global-phase equivalence from coherent branch use.

A reversible gate flips a target bit exactly when two control bits are both1. Assume each control wire is distinct from the target, but allow the two control wires to coincide. Prove the gate is its own inverse and explain what it reduces to when the controls coincide.

On a two-bit string(c,t), consider the update that flips c itself when c=t=1 and otherwise does nothing. Does the familiar self-inverse proof for a two-control target flip remain valid when one control is also the target? Give a concrete collision and explain the lost hypothesis.

Let S and T be Hermitian matrices on one finite system and X a Hermitian matrix on a second system. Prove that H=S tensor X+T tensor I is Hermitian without assuming that S and T commute. Give a counterexample showing that the same conclusion can fail if X is not Hermitian.

A finite row stencil is a list of offset/coefficient pairs. Its matrix entry at row i and column j is the sum of coefficients of every pair with i+offset=j; no modular wrapping is used. Prove that merging repeated offsets by summing their coefficients leaves every matrix entry unchanged. Use the pairs (1,2),(1,-2),(-1,3) to show why list width and the number of nonzero matrix entries need not agree.

exists_core_lq reshapes a core's (Fin 2 x Fin r) column index to a flat Fin (2r) index via a bijection, applies thin LQ, and reindexes back; A = R*Q and Q*Q-transpose = 1 hold with inner dimension min(l, 2r).
absorb A R contracts R into the right bond of A; absorb_slice shows slice(absorb A R, bit) = slice(A, bit) * R, so absorption is per-bit right multiplication that never mixes emitted-bit branches.
evalWith env : Coeff -> Rat is a homomorphism: it fixes constants, reads symbols from env, and commutes with add, mul, neg.

A system-on-n-qubits candidate with a auxiliary qubits has a 2^(n+a) unitary; the signal register is high-order; the explicit product-register branch equals the flattened signal-system block projection.
Prescribed orthonormal columns placed at arbitrary distinct positions via an injection extend to an orthogonal matrix agreeing on those positions.

new_cores.summary: The r < N hypothesis in exists_specialOrthogonal_completion is necessary: a fully-prescribed det=-1 orthonormal frame (e.g. diag(1,-1)) has no determinant-+1 completion, since no unused column remains for the sign-flip repair.
The backward recurrence new left bond = min(l, 2m') gives head_bound (l' <= l and l' <= 2m') and last_bond_le_two (penultimate bond <= 2 when the terminal bond is 1).
A general positive-operator measurement fixes outcome probabilities but not the post-measurement state; orthogonality/idempotency of projectors is what supplies a canonical update.

Positive partial transpose is a necessary separability test certified by a negative eigenvalue; it is also sufficient only when the dimension product is at most 6, with bound entangled states as the converse boundary.
The density operators form a convex set: positivity needs nonnegative weights, unit trace needs the weights to sum to one, and the extreme points are exactly the pure states.
An isometry with orthonormal columns maps one pure-state ensemble of a mixed state to another realizing the same state, proving ensembles are infinitely non-unique.

Product states give independent local outcomes, but separable mixtures can be classically correlated; purity forces a separable state to be a single uncorrelated product, so correlated separable states are necessarily mixed.
The trace norm equals the maximum of |tr(XU)| over unitaries, bounded via SVD and attained at U = V W-dagger; the optimizer depends on X, so the maximization cannot be replaced by any fixed unitary.

A U-tensor-U-invariant two-qubit (Werner) state is entangled exactly when its swap overlap x is negative, proved by a partial-transpose eigenvalue x/2 and a dimension-independent swap-trick separability argument.

Postselecting the all-zeros ancilla of a block encoding succeeds with probability ||A|b>||^2/alpha^2, recovering the lost norm and penalizing oversized subnormalization, while the kept state is the normalized A|b>.

Because any block of a unitary is a contraction, embedding A at factor alpha requires alpha >= ||A||; a unit factor is impossible once ||A|| > 1, and the bound fixes the scale but not an efficient circuit.

Entrywise checks certify an exact unit-factor block encoding and equal the operator identity, but approximate embedding is defined by an operator-norm bound that small per-entry errors can violate after dimensional accumulation.

Any contraction A dilates to a one-ancilla unitary with A as its top-left block via its SVD; because a non-unitary A is no native system-only gate, the ancilla and postselection that absorb the norm loss are unavoidable.

In a prepare-select-unprepare LCU implementation the subnormalization factor ||beta||_2 ||gamma||_2 is bounded below by ||alpha||_1 via Cauchy-Schwarz, attained at the symmetric split sqrt(|alpha_i|), which maximizes the success probability.
Defines the block-encoding projected-block contract: A = alpha*(<0^a| tensor I)U(|0^a> tensor I) exactly, operator-norm epsilon bound approximately, with explicit dimensions.
Success-sector workspace cleanup is an independent promise, not implied by the doubly projected block; a one-qubit rotation supplies a concrete counterexample.
Disjoint clean auxiliary registers compose blocks by matrix multiplication; X/X refutes naive same-register reuse, and neither reset nor inverse is a free coherent repair.
Why the per-split rotation angle carries the sign of the second sibling amplitude, so negative real amplitudes are reproduced exactly rather than as magnitudes.
Only clean fresh-bit-zero columns drive the emitted state, and introducing the fresh zero bit is norm-preserving rather than a postselection.
Canonicalization derives a normalized initial boundary and exact amplitude recovery from only the sum-of-squares-one hypothesis, assuming no target-state equality.
Right-canonicalization concentrates all squared mass in the residual initial boundary while leaving the terminal bond at dimension one.
The low-wire marginal has the same total squared norm as the full table, via the per-pair Pythagorean identity and a last-bit reindexing.
Dividing a real table by the square root of its strictly positive total squared norm yields an exactly unit state, with nonvanishing of the norm the single load-bearing hypothesis.
The sequential run amplitude equals the chronological transfer contraction of the cores applied to the boundary, provable by induction using only clean-column equality.
Unitary sequential stages from a basis boundary keep total probability one at every length, a coherent success with mass-neutral fresh-zero padding and no postselection.
Orthonormal real core rows become orthonormal complex input-bond columns under the output-row/input-column orientation, because realness makes conjugation trivial.
Canonicalization's reduced bonds obey l'=min(l,2m'), yielding a two-sided head bound, a sharp at-most-two penultimate bond for scalar trains, and non-expansion of the maximal bond.

Demanding terminal cleanup on all padded columns forces more orthonormal vectors than a 2-dimensional output subspace admits, so for active dimension > 2 it breaks unitarity; the library restricts the condition to active columns plus a support invariant.
Inactive zero-padded completion columns are gauge freedom: support propagation forces the emitted state to equal the tensor contraction regardless of those columns, refuting an ambiguity claim.

Zero sibling pairs are harmless vanishing subtrees handled by angle zero; only a globally zero vector breaks the normalized first-column identity, so strict positivity of the total norm is the minimal honest hypothesis.
